main_text.l: tantur vafri homines contra omne
fixum & sacrum in Religione & Legibus: quas his
machinulis suis (velut cochlea quadam
adtorquente subtiliter quidem, sed valide)
sensim primò & occulta inflectione à Nota
sua Regula, & consuetudine abducunt,
ut obsequentiores deinde fiant eorum
cupidini, qui sub larva Sacrorum Fœderum,
sibi omnia subjicere moliuntur.
His tamen Funiculis & quasi intorti-
s viminibus haud sperandum est diutius
tenere conscientias, quàm dum Vis illis
adsit plicatrix: statim enim quisque sibi
Pontifex fit, & illa facilè solvit ligamina, quæ
non aliquod è Verbo Divino præceptum, sed
Astutia[?] Factionis, vel Terror indidit; quæque
vel superflua erant prius obligatis, vel
cum fraude & injuria impofita, si eo consi-
lio posterius imponi deprehenderint, ut
justæ illæ priores & necessariæ obligationes, vel
pro tempore ceciderint, vel omnino
diffolvcrentur.

Me-dia ista Illicita ut ad Officium suum melius
adigantur homines, sed ut Partibus accedant
firmiores. Atque adeò parum refert, quid
de piis Fœderum clausulis exequaris,
modò, Consiliis & Partibus, & Principali horum

page.notes: The right-margin mark "s" beside "adhæreas." is uncertain: it may be a reference letter or a signature mark; transcribed as a note but unverified. Greek running head copied as seen; the Greek letters are partly unclear. "Astutia" is uncertain (the first letter looks stylised). Long s was normalised to s throughout (e.g. "sensim", "subjicere", "suum", "consilio", "adsit"); words such as "fit" and "fiant" were read as real f. The paragraph ends mid-sentence at the page foot with no catchword visible. Possible printing errors left as printed: "Iftius", "diffolvcrentur", "Me-dia" is a line-end hyphenation.
